name: Open-set Object Detection (VOC-COCO & OpenImagesRoad)
description: In real-world applications where confidence is key, like autonomous driving, the accurate detection and appropriate handling of classes differing from those used during training are crucial. Despite the proposal of various unknown object detection approaches, we have observed widespread inconsistencies among them regarding the datasets, metrics, and scenarios used, alongside a notable absence of a clear definition for unknown objects, which hampers meaningful evaluation. To counter these issues, we introduce two benchmarks: a unified VOC-COCO evaluation, and the new OpenImagesRoad benchmark which provides clear hierarchical object definition besides new evaluation metrics. Complementing the benchmark, we exploit recent self-supervised Vision Transformers performance, to improve pseudo-labeling-based OpenSet Object Detection (OSOD), through OW-DETR++. State-of-the-art methods are extensively evaluated on the proposed benchmarks. This study provides a clear problem definition, ensures consistent evaluations, and draws new conclusions about effectiveness of OSOD strategies.
evaluation_method: Closed-set mAP for known classes plus open-set specific metrics (unknown-detection F1 / precision-recall / proposed open-set metrics in the paper)
general_score_metric: mAP (for known classes) and open-set detection metrics (unknown-detection F1 / open-set specific metrics proposed by the authors)
typical_sota_score: known-class mAP ~60–80%; unknown-detection F1 typically much lower (≈30–60%) depending on method and thresholding
reputation: An emerging benchmark aiming to standardize open-set object detection evaluation; useful for researchers working on safety-critical detection (e.g., autonomous driving).
notes: Addresses prior inconsistencies by unifying datasets/metrics; non-LLM benchmark. Reported scores can vary significantly by dataset split and unknown-class definition. Potential dataset biases from hierarchical definitions; community adoption is still growing.
